scenes.heading: Persistence and Topologies in 6.5
scenes.narration: Oak & Operations. Persistence and Topologies in 6.5. In this video we review 7 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is Adobe's default persistence recommendation starting with AEM 6.2?
scenes.heading: Use TarMK as the default in all deployments except specific cases
scenes.body: Section 12 says that starting with AEM 6.2, Adobe recommends TarMK as the default in all deployments for both Author and Publish, except for specific cases.

scenes.question: Which statement best describes a single TarMK instance?
scenes.heading: It is one instance on one server, simple and fast, but not scalable beyond that server and without failover
scenes.body: The source says a single TarMK instance is one instance on a single server, is the default for Author, and is simple and fast but has no failover and cannot scale beyond that server.

scenes.question: What is true about TarMK Cold Standby?
scenes.heading: A primary replicates its repository to a standby, failover is not automatic, and both instances need a license
scenes.body: Section 12 says TarMK Cold Standby replicates the primary repository to a standby, the standby runs only the HTTP receiver, failover is not automatic, and both instances need a license.

scenes.question: Why is a TarMK Farm the default for Publish?
scenes.heading: It uses several independent TarMK Oak instances, scales reads, and provides failover
scenes.body: The source says a TarMK Farm consists of several independent Oak instances with TarMK, kept in sync because Author publishes the same content to each member, and that it scales reads and gives failover.

scenes.question: How is an Oak cluster with MongoMK characterized?
scenes.heading: Several Author instances access a MongoDB replica set in an active-active topology that scales Author horizontally and provides high availability
scenes.body: Section 12 says an Oak cluster with MongoMK has several Author instances accessing a MongoDB replica set, works active-active, scales Author horizontally, and provides high availability.

scenes.question: When does the speech say MongoMK on Author should be considered?
scenes.heading: When Author load is very high, such as thousands of named users a day, hundreds of concurrent users, or very large daily asset ingestion, edits, or searches
scenes.body: The source gives MongoMK selection criteria as large-scale Author demands, including thousands of named users a day, hundreds of concurrent users, hundreds of thousands of ingestions or edits a day, and tens of thousands of searches a day.

scenes.question: What minimal MongoDB topology is recommended for a MongoMK Author setup?
scenes.heading: A replica set with one primary and two secondaries under 15 ms latency, plus an Author cluster with two active nodes
scenes.body: Section 12 says the minimal MongoDB topology is a replica set with one primary and two secondaries with latency under 15 milliseconds, along with an Author cluster of two active nodes.

scenes.heading: Quick recap
items: Use TarMK as the default in all deployments except specific cases
It is one instance on one server, simple and fast, but not scalable beyond that server and without failover
A primary replicates its repository to a standby, failover is not automatic, and both instances need a license
It uses several independent TarMK Oak instances, scales reads, and provides failover
Several Author instances access a MongoDB replica set in an active-active topology that scales Author horizontally and provides high availability
When Author load is very high, such as thousands of named users a day, hundreds of concurrent users, or very large daily asset ingestion, edits, or searches
A replica set with one primary and two secondaries under 15 ms latency, plus an Author cluster with two active nodes
scenes.narration: Quick recap of Persistence and Topologies in 6.5. Take a moment to review these 7 key points.
